webAccess.title: Access
webAccess.exposureDescription: Choose whether browsers outside this computer can reach this node. Access is off until you enable and save it.
webAccess.listenAddressHint: A specific IP address assigned to this node and a port, for example 192.168.1.20:50052. Wildcard addresses are not allowed.
webAccess.publicUrlHint: Optional. Leave blank to use the listener address. For internet access through a router, enter the external HTTPS host and port.
webAccess.httpsNotice: HTTPS is always required. Sisyphus creates a self-signed certificate; each browser may need you to accept its certificate warning before pairing and API calls work.

chatAttachmentsNeedNodeUpdate: Update the node before sending chat attachments. This daemon does not support safe chat file ownership.
privateFileWarning: Private files are sealed with private.key. Losing this key permanently loses access. Only private jobs can read them; their workers receive the decryption key. Use trusted workers.
chatAttachmentPrivacyNotice: Attachments are encrypted with private.key; losing it permanently loses access. Private jobs share the key with trusted workers. Chat deletion releases its ownership. Unattached files may be collected after 24 hours; manual uploads and files needed by other chats or jobs remain retained.

modelSettings.title: Model provider
modelSettings.profileDescription: Configure the model provider used by this node’s planner. API keys are stored privately in the node database.
modelSettings.modelManagementDescription: Download models from the configured Ollama endpoint or remove ones you no longer need.
modelSettings.modelManagementEmpty: No models found. Enter a model name above to download one.
modelSettings.removeModelDescription: This permanently removes {model} from this Ollama service. You can download it again later.
modelSettings.hint: Choose the model provider used by the planner. API keys are sent directly to the local daemon and are never displayed again.

providerDescriptions.ollama: Run models on this machine or another Ollama server. Models stay wherever the server runs.
providerDescriptions.anthropic: Use Claude models through Anthropic’s service.
providerDescriptions.openai: Use OpenAI or compatible hosted and self-hosted services, including vLLM, llama.cpp, and LM Studio.

modelSettings.keepKey: Leave empty to keep saved key
modelSettings.optionalApiKey: Optional — leave blank if this server does not require a key
modelSettings.lendingTitle: Lend Ollama models to the pool
modelSettings.lendingDescription: Offer selected models from this Ollama endpoint to trusted pool workers. The endpoint can run on this or another reachable machine.
modelSettings.lendingLiveNote: Model selection and request limits apply live. Enabling, disabling, or changing the Ollama address needs a node restart.
modelSettings.lendingEnabled: Make models from this Ollama endpoint available to the pool
modelSettings.remoteOllamaNote: The worker connects to this remote Ollama endpoint, and pool prompts and inputs are sent there. Hardware reported to the pool still belongs to this node, not the remote server.
modelSettings.remoteOllamaHttpNote: This remote Ollama endpoint uses HTTP. Prompts and inputs sent to it are not encrypted in transit; use HTTPS or a trusted private network.
modelSettings.inspectEmpty: Ollama answered, but no models were found.
modelSettings.allModelsHint: All checked models are offered. To offer none, turn model lending off.
modelSettings.gpuLayers: GPU layers (−1 = as many as fit; 0 = CPU only)
modelSettings.ollamaRestartNote: These settings belong to the Ollama server, not Sisyphus, and require restarting Ollama.
modelSettings.ollamaWindows: Windows: set these in your account’s Environment Variables, then quit and relaunch Ollama.
modelSettings.ollamaMac: macOS: set each with launchctl setenv, then restart the Ollama app.
modelSettings.ollamaLinux: Linux (systemd): add Environment="NAME=value" under [Service] with systemctl edit ollama.service, then reload systemd and restart Ollama.
modelSettings.restartNeeded: Restart to apply lending or address changes
modelSettings.setByFlags: Startup flags currently control model lending. Saved settings will apply only when the node starts without --models-from.

providerKeyRequired: This provider requires an API key. Enter one or use the key saved for this service.
liveDescription: A live view of this machine in the Sisyphus network.
waitingForDaemon: Waiting for the local gRPC API at {endpoint}. Start the daemon to see this node come online.
browserAuthTitle: Connect this browser to your node
browserAuthWaiting: The node is online. Authenticate this browser to continue.
browserAuthDescription: Pair this browser with a one-time code from a browser already connected to the node.
browserHttpWarning: This connection uses plain HTTP. Devices monitoring this network may see pairing codes and sessions. Use only on a trusted local network.
browserTokenAlternative: Use the node API token instead

browserAccess.title: Devices
browserAccess.description: Manage browsers and devices paired with this node. Create a one-time code or QR link to pair another device.
browserAccess.httpWarning: Browsers on other machines reach this node over HTTPS, with a certificate the node made for itself. Each browser warns about it the first time: compare the fingerprint under Settings → Access before accepting, and pair only on a network you trust.
browserAccess.scanCode: Scan this QR code or enter the code on the other device.
browserAccess.codeExpired: This pairing code expired. Create a new one.
browserAccess.noDevices: No devices have been paired yet.

geoCountryAsSeenByPool: Approximate country (as seen by the pool)
unplacedLink: Not placed: turn on location discovery
unplacedHint: This node knows itself only by a home-network address, which no table can place. Asking your router, a STUN server or a lookup service can find its public address.
countryEstimateDisclaimer: An estimate from network address data; may be inaccurate
peerConnectionHint: Connect attempts a direct libp2p connection. Connecting does not authorize the peer to run compute.
onlineListening: This node is online and listening. Peer connections will show up here as they are discovered.
connectDaemon: Connect to the local daemon to see live peer state.
workspaceDescription: Your local node and the peers it currently knows about.
agentEmptyTitle: A smarter compute loop starts here.
agentEmptyDescription: Ask your local Sisyphus planner about this node, the network, or a computation.
agentUnavailableHint: AI provider setup will live on this node.
topologyIllustration: Illustration of this node and its known peers

globeDetails.thisNodeWorksFor: This node is working for it now
globeDetails.name: Name

topologyNote: This is a topology illustration, not a geographic map. It shows peers reported by this node; their real locations are not known.
workspaceFooter: The compute loop will appear here as the node gains planning and execution capabilities.
settingsDescription: Configure this desktop interface and its local-node view.
generalSettingsHint: Language and appearance preferences for this device.
localDaemonSettingsHint: The daemon owns node identity, networking, and runtime configuration.

nodeLocationSettings.title: Where this node is
nodeLocationSettings.description: Put this node on the map yourself. It is the most precise way, and nothing is sent anywhere to find it.
nodeLocationSettings.coordinatesHelp: Latitude and longitude, as a map copies them: right-click a place in OpenStreetMap or Google Maps and copy its coordinates.
nodeLocationSettings.coordinatesInvalid: Enter a latitude from -90 to 90 and a longitude from -180 to 180, such as 37.2710, -79.9414.
nodeLocationSettings.shareHelp: How much of this place other members of a pool may see. This node always knows it exactly.
nodeLocationSettings.pinned: Your pin places this node on your own globe. Your pool sees it only as far as you chose above.
nodeLocationSettings.notPinned: No pin yet. The node places itself as well as its other sources can.
nodeLocationSettings.unavailable: This node's daemon is too old to keep a location. Update it to set one.

cityTableSettings.title: City table
cityTableSettings.description: A free table of Internet addresses and the cities they are in, about 90 MB. With it, this node finds the city it is in from its public address. It is downloaded only when you ask.
cityTableSettings.privacy: Downloading it shows db-ip.com this machine's address. After that, finding the city asks no one: the table is on this computer.
cityTableSettings.accuracy: The city is an estimate, often tens of kilometres off, since an address is placed where its provider's network is. Your own pin wins over it, and it is not sent to your pool.
cityTableSettings.creditLabel: The table's licence asks for this credit:
cityTableSettings.downloading: Downloading and reading the table. It can take a few minutes.
cityTableSettings.downloadFailed: Could not download the city table
cityTableSettings.removeFailed: Could not remove the city table
cityTableSettings.estimate: This node looks to be near {place}.
cityTableSettings.noEstimate: The table does not place this node yet. It needs the node's public address, which the node has not found; Location discovery can help.
cityTableSettings.pinWins: Your pin places this node, so the table's estimate is not used.
cityTableSettings.unavailable: This node's daemon is too old to keep a city table. Update it to download one.

locationDiscoverySettings.title: Location discovery
locationDiscoverySettings.description: Optional sources can help estimate this node’s network location when its own public addresses are unknown.
locationDiscoverySettings.gatewayDescription: Allow a read-only NAT-PMP request to this computer’s default gateway for its external IPv4 address. No port mapping is created; only your gateway receives the request.
locationDiscoverySettings.gatewayUnavailable: Gateway lookup is not available on this operating system.
locationDiscoverySettings.lookupTitle: Use ipapi.co as a last resort
locationDiscoverySettings.lookupDescription: If local, pool, gateway, and configured STUN sources cannot place this node, send its public IP address to ipapi.co. ipapi.co then says which country that address is in.
locationDiscoverySettings.stunDescription: Use only a server you enter. It is contacted only if earlier sources cannot locate this node; the server will see the public IP address that reaches it. No port is opened.
locationDiscoverySettings.stunInvalid: Enter a hostname or IP address, optionally followed by a port from 1 to 65535.
locationDiscoverySettings.operatorManaged: This daemon does not support configuring location discovery here yet. Update it to enable these controls.
locationDiscoverySettings.restartRequired: Saved. Quit and reopen Sisyphus to apply these changes.
locationDiscoverySettings.restartHint: Changes take effect the next time you open Sisyphus.
locationDiscoverySettings.restartDaemonRequired: Saved. Restart the daemon to apply these changes.
locationDiscoverySettings.restartDaemonHint: Changes take effect the next time the daemon starts.

poolHostingSettings.title: Let other machines join this pool
poolHostingSettings.description: Off unless you turn it on. When on, the node this app starts takes workers at the address and port below, so other computers can join the pool it coordinates.
poolHostingSettings.discoveryNote: Hosting also turns on discovery: this node is advertised on the shared Sisyphus network, with its ID and addresses, so other nodes can find it. Being found admits no one. A machine joins only with an invitation from this pool, and the app’s own control connection stays on this computer.
poolHostingSettings.notManaged: This app is connected to a node it did not start. That node takes workers wherever its --listen option says, so this setting does not apply to it.
poolHostingSettings.addressUnavailable: This pool is not open to other machines: {address} is not one of this computer’s addresses now. The node is listening only on this computer. Choose another address and reopen Sisyphus.
poolHostingSettings.addressDescription: The address other machines use to reach this pool. Choose the one on the network they share with this computer.
poolHostingSettings.allInterfacesWarning: Every network this computer is on can reach the pool port, including a VPN or a public Wi-Fi network.
poolHostingSettings.addressRequired: Choose the address other machines should use to reach this pool.
poolHostingSettings.portDescription: The port workers connect to. 7700 unless something else on this computer uses it. A firewall must let other machines reach it.
poolHostingSettings.portInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 65535.
poolHostingSettings.restartRequired: Saved. Quit and reopen Sisyphus to apply these changes.
poolHostingSettings.restartHint: Changes take effect the next time you open Sisyphus.

containerSettings.title: Run containers for the pool
containerSettings.description: Off unless you turn it on. When on, the node this app starts runs container work for the pool with Docker: video re-encoding, molecular dynamics and container jobs.
containerSettings.notManaged: This app is connected to a node it did not start. That node runs containers only if its owner started it with --containers, so this setting does not apply to it.
containerSettings.unavailable: Containers are turned on, but Docker did not answer when the node started, so it is running without them. Start Docker, then restart the node.
containerSettings.dockerNote: Needs Docker: Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS, which is free for personal use, or Docker Engine on Linux.
containerSettings.dockerMissing: Docker is not installed on this computer. Install it, start it and check again.
containerSettings.dockerStopped: Docker is installed but not answering. Start Docker Desktop, or the Docker service, and check again.
containerSettings.trustWarning: Anyone who may submit jobs to this pool can run a container image of their choosing on this computer, within the limits below.
containerSettings.networkTitle: Allow tasks to use the network
containerSettings.networkDescription: Off: a task cannot reach the network or this computer’s local network. Turn it on only for jobs you trust that need it. Re-encoding video and molecular dynamics do not.
containerSettings.readOnlyDescription: A task can write only to its output and to /tmp, which is held in memory. Re-encoding video and molecular dynamics work this way.
containerSettings.tmpDescription: The most a task may write to /tmp. It is held in memory, so keep it below what this computer can spare.
containerSettings.tmpInvalid: Enter a whole number of megabytes from 1 to {max}.
containerSettings.restartRequired: Saved. Restart the node to apply these changes.
containerSettings.restartHint: Changes take effect the next time the node starts.

poolHostingOverview.title: Other machines join this pool here
poolHostingOverview.description: Give a worker this address with --coordinator, together with an invitation from Operations → Pool.
poolHostingOverview.noAddresses: This computer has no network address other machines could use right now.
poolHostingOverview.windowsFirewall: If Windows Firewall blocks workers, run this once in PowerShell opened as administrator. It lets machines on private networks reach the pool port, and nothing else:
poolHostingOverview.firewall: Workers need incoming TCP connections on port {port} allowed by this computer’s firewall.
poolHostingOverview.unavailable: Other machines cannot join: {address} is not one of this computer’s addresses now. Choose another in Settings → This node and reopen Sisyphus.

restartNode.restarted: Node restarted with the saved settings
restartNode.reconnectTimeout: The node did not reconnect within 30 seconds.
restartNode.confirmDescription: Jobs running here: {jobs}. Workers connected: {workers}. Restarting stops this node’s jobs in progress and disconnects its workers; the pool reschedules unfinished tasks when the node is back.

tray.stillRunningBody: Your node keeps working for its pool. Open or quit Sisyphus from its icon in the system tray or menu bar.

poolLimitsSettings.title: Pool limits
poolLimitsSettings.description: What each other member of this node’s pool may use here while this node coordinates the pool. Leave a field empty for no limit. Saved limits apply when the node restarts. Work this node submits itself is not limited.
poolLimitsSettings.unitsNote: Sizes use decimal units: 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes, 1 GB = 1,000 MB, 1 TB = 1,000 GB.
poolLimitsSettings.jobsDescription: How many unfinished jobs one member may have at once.
poolLimitsSettings.tasksDescription: How many unfinished tasks, waiting or running, one member may have across all of its jobs.
poolLimitsSettings.timeoutDescription: How long one attempt at a member’s task may run before it is stopped and tried again. A job may ask for less.
poolLimitsSettings.storeDescription: The most one member may keep in this node’s store.
poolLimitsSettings.uploadDescription: The most a worker may upload for one attempt at a task.
poolLimitsSettings.invalidCount: Enter a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, or leave it empty for no limit.
poolLimitsSettings.invalidDuration: Enter a number of 0 or more that comes to whole seconds, or leave it empty for no limit.
poolLimitsSettings.invalidBytes: Enter a number of 0 or more that comes to whole bytes, or leave it empty for no limit.
poolLimitsSettings.notCoordinator: This node does not run the coordinator role, so these limits have no effect until it does. You can still save them.
poolLimitsSettings.operatorManaged: This daemon does not support configuring pool limits here yet. Update it to enable these controls.
poolLimitsSettings.restartRequired: Saved. Quit and reopen Sisyphus to apply these changes.
poolLimitsSettings.restartHint: Changes take effect the next time you open Sisyphus.
poolLimitsSettings.restartDaemonRequired: Saved. Restart the daemon to apply these changes.
poolLimitsSettings.restartDaemonHint: Changes take effect the next time the daemon starts.

runPage.loading: Loading what this pool can run

runPage.otherWorkloadsDescription: These take their parameters as JSON. Submit them from Operations.
runPage.noWorkerHint: No worker in this pool runs this workload yet, so it cannot start now.
runPage.completeForm: Fill in the required fields to run this.

primes.title: Count primes
primes.description: Counts the prime numbers in a range, split across the pool.

wordcount.title: Count words
wordcount.description: Counts how often each word occurs in a text file.

transcode.title: Re-encode video
transcode.description: Re-encodes a video as H.264, in stretches that different workers encode.

render.title: Render a 3D scene
render.description: Renders a Blender scene with Cycles or EEVEE, by frames or by strips of one frame, across the pool.

transcribe.title: Transcribe speech
transcribe.description: Turns the speech in a recording into text and subtitles, in stretches across the pool.

qchem.title: Compute molecules
qchem.description: Finds the energies, optimised geometries or frequencies of a file of conformers or molecules with xtb, in runs across the pool.

ocr.title: Read text from scans
ocr.description: Reads the text in a scanned PDF or picture with Tesseract, in runs of pages across the pool, as plain text or a searchable PDF.

traj.title: Analyse trajectories
traj.description: Finds RMSD, radius of gyration, distances, hydrogen bonds, secondary structure or RMSF along molecular dynamics trajectories with cpptraj, in runs of frames across the pool.

md.title: Simulate a molecule
md.description: Runs molecular dynamics as replicas across the pool.
